newsitem.title: USA: US stock promoter pleads guilty to fraud, bribery.
newsitem.headline: US stock promoter pleads guilty to fraud, bribery.

text.p: An Illnois stock promoter pled guilty on Monday to wire fraud and bribery in connection with a scheme to fraudently promote the over-the-counter common stock of a Canadian company, federal prosecutors said.

Edward Padnos of Highland Park, Illinois is alleged to have promoted the stock of Cam-Net Communications Network, Inc, of Vancouver, British Columbia by offering to make secret payments to undercover FBI agents.
Padnos is one of eight defendants who have been convicted on charges stemming from this particular FBI sting investigation of fraud in the penny stock market.

The one count superseding indictment charged that Padnos and his co-conspirators offered to make secret payments to undercover FBI agents who were posing as corrupt securities brokers to induce them to make open market purchases of Cam-Net common stock for their customers.
The indictment also alleged that Padnos met with undercover agents in New York City and Atlanta, Georgia to negotiate the size and manner of the secret payments.
Padnos is alleged to have offered to wire cash to an offshore account designated by the agents.

In pleading guilty in Manhattan Federal Court before U.S. District Judge Deborah Batts, Padnos admitted that in March 1996, he agreed with a co-conspirator to arrange a secret payment of cash to the undercover agent equal to 20 percent of the value of any Cam-Net stock purchased.

He also admitted that he arranged the Georgia meeting to discuss the size of the payment and knew that a co-conspirator had paid the agent $3,850 in return for the purchase of $22,000 of Cam-Net common stock.
Padnos faces up to five years in prison and substantial fines when he is sentenced on Nov. 24.
